mitigation_principle: Review peak capacity for critical services; reserve adequate capacity for traffic spikes; introduce fallback mechanisms for non‑critical service failures; implement automated scaling; monitor capacity thresholds

original_source: Confluence page load errors
failure_pattern: An unexpected traffic spike overloaded a non‑critical backend service that was not provisioned with sufficient capacity. The service failure was treated as severe, causing downstream page rendering failures and resulting in page load errors for users.
mitigation_principle: Review peak capacity allocation for critical backend services; reserve adequate capacity for traffic spikes; implement fallback mechanisms for non‑critical service failures; enable automated scaling and capacity monitoring.

original_source: Issues accessing Jira and Confluence in some regions
symptoms: access failures to Jira and Confluence sites
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the regional load balancer caused intermittent routing failures for Jira and Confluence services, leading to authentication and content access errors for affected customers.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks and circuit breakers for regional load balancers; add redundancy and failover routing; monitor traffic patterns and alert on routing anomalies; maintain a rollback plan for configuration changes; enforce configuration validation and peer review before deployment

original_source: Issues loading Administration across Atlassian Products
failure_pattern: A configuration issue caused the Administration page to fail rendering, resulting in a blank page for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks for critical pages; add monitoring for page load failures; enforce configuration validation before deployment; maintain rollback procedures; conduct post-mortem reviews

original_source: Administration is unreachable
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the access control settings caused the Administration service to reject all requests with a 403 error, rendering the interface unreachable for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; add health checks for access control; enforce least privilege; maintain rollback plan; monitor access logs for anomalies

original_source: Issues with authentication across multiple services
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the authentication service caused it to return 503 gateway errors, leading to authentication failures across multiple applications.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks for authentication endpoints; enforce configuration validation before deployment; add circuit breaker to prevent cascading failures; monitor authentication error rates and set alerts.

original_source: Smart Answers in Search and AI Definitions outage for Atlassian Intelligence customers
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration during the rollout of a hotfix caused intermittent errors in the Smart Answers and AI definitions services, leading to an outage for Confluence Cloud Atlassian Intelligence customers. The issue was identified and a fix was progressively rolled out, restoring service within a few hours.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation before deployment; use canary releases with health checks; monitor error rates and rollback automatically; maintain a rollback plan; ensure proper testing of hotfixes.

original_source: Attachment Loading Issue in C2C and Sandbox Migrations
failure_pattern: During the scheduled C2C and Sandbox data copy migrations, the attachment loader failed to retrieve attachments due to a misconfigured storage path, causing attachments to not load in migrated projects. The issue persisted until the migration completed, after which manual deletion and re-run of migration resolved the problem.
mitigation_principle: Validate attachment storage configuration before migration; run automated attachment integrity checks after migration; implement rollback or re-migration strategy for affected projects; document migration procedures and failure handling

original_source: Forge invocation errors impacting some instances in Singapore region
failure_pattern: Forge invocation errors caused marketplace apps to fail, leading to failures across multiple Confluence and Jira features, including content access, authentication, search, and mobile app functionality, affecting users in Singapore region.
mitigation_principle: Implement health checks and circuit breakers for forge service; add automated monitoring and alerting for invocation failures; perform thorough regression testing before deployment; maintain redundancy and failover for critical services; document and review configuration changes

original_source: Issues affecting user syncing, Atlassian Administration
symptoms: errors loading Users and Groups pages
failure_pattern: A failure in the third‑party identity provider caused user IDP sync to fail, which cascaded into errors loading Users and Groups pages across Atlassian Administration services, leading to authentication and user management disruptions.
mitigation_principle: Implement health checks and circuit breakers for third‑party IDP services; add automated monitoring and alerting for sync failures; enforce configuration validation and automated rollback; conduct regular sync testing in staging; improve error handling and user feedback

original_source: Search functionality degradation in Confluence
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the search service caused the search index to be partially unavailable for users in Europe, leading to degraded search performance and incomplete results. The issue was identified and resolved by correcting the configuration and restarting the service.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; add region-specific health checks; monitor search latency per region; enforce rollback procedures; use canary deployments.

original_source: Degraded experience adding and accessing media attachments
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the media storage service caused increased latency and timeouts for attachment uploads and retrievals, leading to degraded user experience across content view and edit operations.
mitigation_principle: Implement health checks and monitoring for media storage latency; enforce rate limiting; add circuit breaker; use automated alerts; test configuration changes in staging; maintain redundancy; document fallback strategy

original_source: Intermittent failure in Forge app invocation
symptoms: app functionality failures across Confluence, Jira, Compass
failure_pattern: Intermittent failures in Forge app invocation caused by a misconfiguration in the app invocation service, leading to failures in smart links and scheduled triggers across multiple Atlassian Cloud products. The issue was detected between 5:44 and 7:44 UTC, mitigated by replaying triggers and applying fixes, after which normal operation resumed.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks for app invocation endpoints; add circuit breaker patterns; enforce stricter configuration validation; monitor scheduled trigger execution; replay triggers on failure; maintain rollback plan

original_source: Product invitation emails not being correctly sent to users
symptoms: product invitation emails not sent to users
failure_pattern: A recent deployment introduced a change that disabled the email notification for product invitations. The change was rolled back, but during the rollback period, emails were not sent, causing users to miss invitation emails. After rollback, emails resumed.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated tests for email notifications; use feature flags for email sending; add monitoring for email delivery metrics; require code review for changes affecting email services; ensure rollback procedures include verification of side effects

original_source: Degraded performance in Confluence and Jira for Microsoft Edge users
symptoms: degraded performance in Confluence and Jira
failed content loading for View Content, Create/Edit, and Comments
failure_pattern: Microsoft Edge 140’s Strict tracking prevention misclassified Atlassian domains as advertising, blocking media and content requests and causing degraded performance in Confluence and Jira for users until Microsoft released a browser update or users changed settings.
mitigation_principle: Implement comprehensive browser compatibility testing; monitor third‑party browser feature changes; provide clear user guidance for workarounds; maintain fallback content delivery mechanisms; coordinate with browser vendors for timely updates

original_source: Degraded performance to multiple Atlassian experiences
failure_pattern: A faulty CDN hostname configuration was deployed, overwriting the existing customer‑serving resource, causing TLS handshake failures and subsequent 503/403 errors for Atlassian services until the change was rolled back.
mitigation_principle: Implement stricter pre‑deployment validation for CDN configurations; enforce immutable hostname policies; use automated conflict detection; perform staged rollouts; add monitoring for configuration drift

original_source: Issues for some partners using Connect Javascript APIs
failure_pattern: An unintended deprecation of ACJS methods linked to retired V1 APIs caused 410 errors for partners using Connect Javascript APIs, leading to service disruption for Marketplace Apps.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated deprecation checks; enforce strict versioning and backward compatibility; add automated tests for deprecated endpoints; monitor API usage and alert on unexpected errors; conduct thorough code reviews for deprecation changes

original_source: Atlassian Cloud Services impacted
symptoms: support portal message to use temporary channel
failure_pattern: An outage at AWS disrupted Atlassian Cloud services, causing service outages and preventing support ticket creation; Atlassian teams monitored the situation and communicated updates while AWS restored services, leading to partial recovery and eventual full restoration.
mitigation_principle: Implement multi-cloud redundancy; add automated failover and health checks; monitor third-party provider status and SLA compliance; diversify infrastructure; establish robust incident response and communication plans

original_source: Degraded performance of Atlassian cloud sites for some customers
failure_pattern: A rollout of new CDN hardware by the infrastructure provider introduced performance regressions on edge servers in several regions, causing increased latency and degraded page loads for Atlassian cloud services; the rollout was halted and reverted, restoring service.
mitigation_principle: 1. Implement automated rollback on performance regression detection; 2. Monitor regional performance metrics during rollouts; 3. Coordinate change management with third-party providers; 4. Use staged rollouts with canary testing; 5. Establish performance baselines and alerts.

original_source: Delay in execution of Automation rules
failure_pattern: AWS outage caused scaling issues in our infrastructure, leading to insufficient resources for the Automation service, which resulted in delayed execution of Automation rules.
mitigation_principle: Implement auto-scaling thresholds; add circuit breaker patterns; monitor resource utilization; add redundancy; perform failover testing; add alerting for scaling events

original_source: Interruption to Confluence in APSE region
failure_pattern: A sudden spike in database load caused Confluence backend to become unresponsive in the APSE region, leading to failures in viewing, creating, and editing content. The issue was mitigated by addressing the load and monitoring performance, after which availability recovered.
mitigation_principle: 1. Implement database load monitoring and alerting; 2. Set up auto-scaling for database replicas; 3. Apply rate limiting on write operations; 4. Use caching for read-heavy operations; 5. Conduct load testing before deployments

original_source: Unable to perform UI Operations
symptoms: unable to create or update automation rules
429 status codes for automation API calls
root_cause_category: resource exhaustion due to misconfigured internal service
failure_pattern: An internal service generated excessive traffic, exceeding the API Gateway rate limits. The throttling caused 429 errors and prevented automation rule creation and webhook execution, leading to UI failures for customers.
mitigation_principle: 1. Increase API Gateway rate limits and set appropriate quotas; 2. Disable or throttle the internal service causing high traffic; 3. Implement circuit breakers and rate limiting on internal services; 4. Add monitoring and alerting for traffic spikes; 5. Conduct root cause analysis and apply configuration fixes.

original_source: Degraded performance and intermittent errors
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the Automation UI service caused increased latency and intermittent errors for users of Confluence, Jira Service Management, and Jira Cloud, leading to degraded performance. The issue was resolved after correcting the configuration.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; add health checks for UI latency; set up real-time monitoring and alerting; perform regression testing before deployment; enforce configuration change approvals
